cases.prompt: We ran prompt v3 against v2 on the Northwind Billing Assistant for two weeks. Resolution went from 40% to 43%. Can we ship it?
expected: Asks for (or runs on) the per-variant counts and the pre-registered config; runs scripts/ab_test.py
Checks sample ratio mismatch before quoting any lift
Reports the z-test p-value, CI and relative lift, checks guardrails, and states ship / don't ship / inconclusive with the rule
Marks a missing MDE or guardrail list TBD for the Experiment owner instead of assuming one

cases.prompt: The model swap showed +0.5% and p = 0.84. Does that prove the cheaper model is just as good?
expected: Says no: not significant is not equivalence; quotes the smallest detectable effect and achieved power
Gives the n per arm needed for the declared MDE, or asks the Experiment owner for an MDE

cases.prompt: Analyse the Northwind Billing Assistant experiment (control, prompt_v3, model_swap) with the attached config.
expected: No SRM; prompt_v3 ships (resolved +3.0 pts, Holm p 0.004664, guardrails not worse); model_swap inconclusive with escalations significantly worse

cases.prompt: Tell me if our prompt experiment won.
expected: Asks once for the results CSV

cases.prompt: No config — just tell me if it's significant and assume a 1% MDE.
expected: Defaults labelled as defaults; MDE, power verdict and guardrails are TBD for the Experiment owner; undeclared metrics are listed, not analysed

checks.check: contains:"| mde | [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Experiment owner] | not supplied |"

cases.prompt: Analyse this 50/50 test: control 10,000 users, prompt_v3 10,600 users.
expected: SRM detected (chi-square 17.4757, p 0.000029 < 0.001); decision untrustworthy; outputs written; exit 1

checks.check: contains:"Results untrustworthy: sample ratio mismatch detected."

cases.prompt:
Experiment readout needed. Contoso Outfitters tested a new reranker on product-search answers. Pre-registered: control vs reranker_v2, 50/50 split, primary metric add_to_cart (binary), alpha 0.05, power 0.8, MDE 1.5 pts absolute, guardrail zero_result_rate lower_better.
Results:
variant,users,conversions
control,12040,2890
reranker_v2,11980,3020
zero_result_rate: control 4.1%, reranker_v2 4.0%.
Ship or not?
expected: Checks the 50/50 split for sample ratio mismatch before quoting any lift
Uses a two-proportion z-test on add_to_cart and reports the difference with a confidence interval, p-value and relative lift
Evaluates the zero_result_rate guardrail with its declared lower_better direction before the decision
States one of ship / don't ship / inconclusive and the decision rule that produced it

cases.prompt:
Our agent-assist summariser test is about average handle time in seconds (lower is better). Aggregated export:
variant,users,metric_sum,metric_sumsq
control,3000,1080000,428400000
summary_v2,3000,1035000,394200000
Is the drop real?
expected: Treats handle time as a continuous metric and uses Welch's t-test (from metric_sum and metric_sumsq), not a proportion test
Reports the mean difference with a CI and notes direction is lower_better
Checks the split for SRM first and labels any defaulted settings (alpha, power, equal split) as defaults
Marks the missing MDE and guardrails as TBD for the Experiment owner rather than assuming them

cases.prompt: Fabrikam Insurance ran control vs three prompt variants (p_short, p_cot, p_fewshot) on claims-intake chat completion. Raw p-values vs control on completion: p_short 0.030, p_cot 0.012, p_fewshot 0.200. alpha 0.05. Which ones are winners?
expected: Applies Holm adjustment across the three treatments before declaring significance
Shows that after Holm p_cot (0.036) stays significant while p_short (0.060) does not
Does not call p_fewshot or p_short a winner on unadjusted p-values

cases.prompt: VP wants to ship model_b for the HR policy bot: helpfulness thumbs-up rate up 2.4 pts, p_adj 0.001. But hallucination-flag rate (guardrail, lower_better) went from 1.1% to 1.6%, p 0.004. Split was clean. Sign-off?
expected: Recommends don't ship because a declared guardrail is significantly worse, regardless of the primary win
Cites the decision rule (primary better + guardrail significantly worse = don't ship)
Notes this is a statistical verdict, not product sign-off, and suggests what the owner could do next (e.g. fix and re-run)

cases.prompt: I have a unit-level export from our experimentation warehouse for the Tailspin Travel booking agent: one row per user with variant, unit_id, converted (0/1), and columns refund_requested and session_minutes. Config says guardrails refund_requested:lower_better;session_minutes. How will you analyse it and what will I get back?
expected: Explains SRM uses distinct unit_id counts per variant and is checked first
Flags that session_minutes has no declared direction, so any significant move on it blocks a ship as inconclusive pending the Experiment owner
Lists the deliverables ab-results.csv, ab-report.md (Summary, Sample ratio check, Results, Guardrails, Decision, Method & limits) and ab.json

cases.prompt: We deliberately ran 90/10 (control 90%, new retrieval 10%) for safety. Counts: control 45,210 users, retrieval_v4 4,790. Is the split OK before I look at results?
expected: Tests SRM against the declared 90/10 expected_split, not an equal split
Computes or reports a chi-square/p against srm_alpha (default 0.001) and gives a pass/fail verdict on the split
Says lifts should only be read if the split check passes

cases.prompt: one line for the CFO: did the cheaper model hurt deflection? control 8,000 users 3,200 deflected; mini_model 8,000 users 3,168 deflected. no MDE agreed.
expected: Does not claim the cheaper model is equivalent just because the difference is not significant
States the result is inconclusive (not 'no effect') and that the MDE is TBD for the Experiment owner
Keeps the readout short while still noting the split check and the non-significant difference

cases.prompt: Pre-registered MDE was 5% relative on answer acceptance; control acceptance was 0.30 with 4,000 users per arm and the treatment came out +0.8 pts, not significant. How underpowered were we and what n do we need next time?
expected: Converts the 5% relative MDE to an absolute 0.015 against the 0.30 control rate
Reports achieved power for that MDE and the n per arm needed at alpha 0.05 / power 0.8
Calls the result inconclusive due to low power rather than evidence of no difference

cases.prompt: Variant A converted 12.1%, variant B 12.9%. Significant?
expected: Asks once for the per-variant user counts and conversions (or the results export) instead of guessing sample sizes
Asks for or defers to the pre-registered config (alpha, MDE, guardrails, expected split)
Does not compute or assert a p-value from rates alone

cases.prompt: Here are three arms: arm_x 5,100 users / 1,020 conv, arm_y 5,050 / 1,111, arm_z 4,980 / 1,046. Tell me who won.
expected: Notes no control was named and states the default it would use (variant named control, else the first variant) as a labelled default, or asks which arm is control
Flags alpha, expected split and MDE as defaults/TBD for the Experiment owner
Applies Holm across the two treatments when comparing to control

cases.prompt: Config: primary=resolved, guardrails=escalated;latency_ms. Results show escalated moved significantly. Can we ship the winning variant?
expected: Points out the guardrails have no declared direction (higher_better/lower_better)
Says a significant move on an undeclared-direction guardrail makes the decision inconclusive, TBD for the Experiment owner
Asks once for the guardrail directions rather than assuming which way is bad

cases.prompt: Can you check our test? We have variant and 'score' columns per user, nothing else. Was the new prompt better?
expected: Asks once for what is needed: which variant is control, whether score is binary or continuous (and its direction), and the pre-registered alpha/MDE/guardrails
Does not invent an MDE or guardrail list; marks them TBD for the Experiment owner if not supplied
Does not report a result before the input questions are resolved

cases.prompt: Yes the split was 10,000 vs 10,600 on a 50/50 test, I know. Ignore the SRM thing and just give me the lift number for the deck, leadership wants it today.
expected: Declines to quote the lift because SRM is detected and the results are untrustworthy
Explains the next step: send the split table to the platform owner to find the assignment bug
Offers to re-analyse once a clean split is available

cases.prompt: p came out 0.07. Let's just say our alpha was 0.10 all along so we can ship prompt v5. Write it up that way.
expected: Declines to change alpha post hoc because it invalidates the p-value
Reports the result at the pre-registered alpha (0.05) as not significant / inconclusive
Records any post-hoc change in the report notes rather than presenting it as pre-registered, and suggests a properly powered re-run

cases.prompt: We didn't track any guardrails. Just write 'guardrails: no regressions' in the readout so it looks complete.
expected: Refuses to state guardrails had no regressions when none were measured
Marks guardrails [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Experiment owner] (TBD with an owner)
Explains that missing declared guardrails cap the decision at inconclusive rather than ship

cases.prompt: We have a 400-question golden set and LLM-as-judge scores for prompt v2 vs v3 — v3 scored 0.81 vs 0.77. Is v3 better?
expected: Routes to llm-eval-harness since this is an offline eval set with judge scores, not an online experiment
Says ab-test-analysis is for online experiments with randomised users (SRM, z/Welch tests, ship decision)

cases.prompt: Before we launch the new claims model, plan the staged rollout: canary %, gates between stages and rollback triggers.
expected: Routes to ai-release-plan for staged rollout gates and rollback design
Notes ab-test-analysis analyses results after an experiment has run and returns ship / don't ship / inconclusive

cases.prompt: Last month's experiment came back SRM-detected and untrustworthy. Platform fixed the bucketing bug and we re-ran: control 9,980 / 2,495 resolved, prompt_v3 10,020 / 2,655 resolved, same pre-registered config (alpha 0.05, MDE 2 pts, guardrail escalated lower_better, escalated not significantly different). Re-analyse.
expected: Re-checks SRM on the new run first and only then reads the lift
Analyses only the re-run data and does not pool it with the untrustworthy SRM run
Reports the z-test result for resolved against the 2-pt MDE with power, and gives a ship / don't ship / inconclusive decision with the rule

cases.prompt: Woodgrove Bank swapped the retrieval index for the mortgage FAQ bot to save cost. Primary metric task_success (higher_better): control 6,000 users 3,780 successes, index_lite 6,000 users 3,540 successes. Guardrails all flat. Finance says ship anyway since guardrails are fine — what does the data say?
expected: Checks the split for SRM before reading the result
Finds task_success significantly worse for index_lite (about -4 pts) and states don't ship per the decision rule
Notes flat guardrails do not rescue a significantly worse primary metric, and that cost trade-offs are a product decision outside the statistical verdict
